# LifeContext

> Your documents, compiled. Every claim cited. LifeContext gives Claude Code, Codex and other AI agents your contracts, letters, scans and notes. A local service and the `lifecontext` CLI keep your original files on your machine, extract their text (with local OCR), index them with the open-source Hindsight memory engine, send the text only to the model you choose, and compile a Markdown wiki in an Obsidian vault. Every claim is a literal quote, checked against the source text before the page is written, and cited to its page or passage and the source version; the short summary above the claims is labelled as model-written. Source-available under BUSL-1.1: free for one person for their own use, including at work; businesses need a commercial licence.

For people who work with AI agents and keep documents that matter: leases, contracts, insurance, tax and medical letters, research PDFs, scans in English, Ukrainian or Russian. Not for: people who want an app with no computer to run it on, teams that want one shared knowledge base, or people who need audio, video or web capture.

Current version: 1.2. Platforms: Linux x86_64 and aarch64 (glibc 2.35 or later) and macOS 14 or later on arm64 natively; Windows through Docker or WSL.

## What it does

- Keeps original files immutable, checksummed and versioned. A correction adds a new version.
- Extracts text from TXT, Markdown, PDF (including book-length PDFs), DOCX, XLSX, PPTX and images. Scans go through local Tesseract OCR for English, Ukrainian and Russian. An optional vision model that the owner configures can read handwriting, photos and charts; it is off by default.
- Indexes everything with the Hindsight memory engine (MIT, by Vectorize). LifeContext configures a multilingual reranker for English, Ukrainian and Russian text. LifeContext is built on Hindsight and is not affiliated with Vectorize; no endorsement is implied.
- Compiles a maintained wiki from imported documents. Each document gets its own page. Shared topic and entity pages collect claims from several documents and link to each other. Every claim is a literal quote with a citation to source, version and passage. A short summary above the quotes is labelled as model-written.
- Records the contradictions the model finds between sources and never resolves them automatically.
- Marks pages stale when a source they depend on is corrected or forgotten; `lifecontext wiki rebuild` rebuilds them.
- Writes a daily brief and a change log; `lifecontext wiki lint` reports stale pages, open contradictions, orphan pages and gaps without changing anything.
- Projects pages as Markdown into an Obsidian vault. Each page has a section for the owner's notes, kept byte for byte; edits to the generated part are reported as conflicts instead of being overwritten.
- Also: a journal (notes put in the vault's `Journal/Inbox`, taken in when capture is on, or written by an agent), indexed and searchable next to the documents; compiling the journal into wiki pages comes in v1.3. Export and import bundles, backup and restore.
- Several devices: optional and advanced. The Self-hosted LiveSync Obsidian plugin can sync the vault through a hub on the same machine, reached over Tailscale ([sync guide](https://github.com/rundax/lifecontext/blob/main/docs/sync.md)).

## Agents and models

- One agent skill for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Hermes (`lifecontext skills install`).
- An MCP server (`lifecontext mcp`, stdio) for MCP clients such as Claude Desktop and Cursor, new in 1.2. It is read-only by default; `--allow-writes` lets clients capture and import. Desktop apps do not read the shell PATH, so configure the full path from `command -v lifecontext`.
- Connected agents run the CLI with the owner's authority. The skill tells them what not to do; LifeContext does not enforce per-agent permissions.
- Bring your own model: one at a time, with no default. The installer and `lifecontext init` ask the user to choose Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, a local model server (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio) or another OpenAI-compatible endpoint; unattended installs set `LIFECONTEXT_PROVIDER` and `LIFECONTEXT_MODEL`. With Anthropic, `claude-sonnet-5` works and `claude-haiku-5-5` costs less; Claude Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 do not work yet.

## What leaves the machine

Runs on your machine. Originals never leave it. Extracted text goes to the model provider you choose; with a local model it stays on your machine (supported, not yet part of release qualification). Page images go to a vision model only if you turn one on.

In detail: all extracted text and journal entries go to the provider in chunks when they are indexed, and passages go again when pages are compiled, with the prompts for both. Separately, the first start downloads the embedding and rerank models once.

## What LifeContext does not claim

- No compliance certification or third-party security audit.
- The quote check proves the quoted text exists in the text LifeContext extracted from the source. It does not prove that OCR or a vision model read the original correctly (model-read text is labelled), that a summary is right, that the best quotes were chosen, or that the source is correct.
- Not every contradiction is found. The model proposes them while compiling; LifeContext records them but can miss some.
- No benchmark comparisons against other products.

## Licence

Source-available under the Business Source License 1.1 (BUSL-1.1).

Free for one person who runs their own copy for their own use, at home or at work, including documents that belong to your employer or your clients, and work as a freelancer or sole proprietor. Also free for non-profit organizations, accredited educational institutions and non-profit or publicly funded research institutions. A commercial licence is needed when a business installs, provides or manages LifeContext for its staff or others, or when anyone offers it (or a derivative) to others as a hosted, managed or embedded service. Reading, evaluating and testing the code is free for everyone. Each release becomes Apache-2.0 on or before its Change Date (2030-11-08 for 1.2.0).

- Free: your own notes and documents; your work laptop and your employer's documents (the licence does not override your employer's confidentiality rules, including for text sent to your model provider); freelance client work, where the reports you deliver are your work.
- Commercial licence: your employer installs or manages LifeContext for a team; a shared company instance; a hosted service.
- Commercial licences: roman@rundax.com. Details and more examples: [LICENSING.md](https://github.com/rundax/lifecontext/blob/main/LICENSING.md).

## Install

- Script: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/rundax/lifecontext/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh` (checks SHA256SUMS and, with cosign 3 or later, its signature; installs dependencies from a lock with pinned hashes; asks which model to use, with no default, and checks it with a short probe; runs `init`, `service install --maintenance`, `skills install` and `doctor`; installs Tesseract through Homebrew on macOS, or through apt, dnf or pacman only when sudo works without a password, and otherwise prints the command; a re-run stops the service, backs up, upgrades and starts it again). Then: open the vault folder in Obsidian, `lifecontext documents import ~/Documents/lease.pdf`, and ask your agent about the document.
- Docker image: `ghcr.io/rundax/lifecontext:1.2.0` (runs as uid 1000; volumes `/data/home` and `/data/vault`; the key as a Compose secret or a file mounted at `/run/secrets/lifecontext_api_key`; `LIFECONTEXT_PROVIDER` and `LIFECONTEXT_MODEL` are required on the first start, other `LIFECONTEXT_*` settings optional; no published port; use `docker compose exec lifecontext lifecontext ...`; agents on the host use the `bin/lifecontext-docker` wrapper)
- From source, with Python 3.12: `git clone https://github.com/rundax/lifecontext.git`, then `uv pip install -c constraints-cpu.txt --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu --index-strategy unsafe-best-match -e .` on Linux (`uv pip install -e .` on macOS), then `lifecontext init`, `lifecontext preflight --model-probe`, `lifecontext service install --maintenance`, `lifecontext skills install`, `lifecontext doctor`
- Resources: about 3 GB of disk for the runtime and models (measured in CI on Linux: 2.4 GB installation, 0.6 GB models). Recall reranks on the CPU; expect tens of seconds on a 4-core machine.
